status: Working interpretation of the team decisions supplied on 2026-09-12; Andrew's confirmation is pending.

labels.name: Preventing/slowing ageing
labels.description: The stated aim studies biological ageing itself or develops/tests ways to modify it. This working definition includes fundamental mechanisms of ageing, even without a therapy. Model organisms qualify when biological ageing is the research aim. A drug name, cellular senescence in a tumour, or a background reference to ageing is not enough.

labels.name: Fighting the consequences of ageing
labels.description: The stated aim concerns age-related disease, functional decline, care, or social and population consequences of ageing. It must establish the ageing connection. Treating a disease in older adults does not by itself target ageing biology. Generic disease research without that connection does not qualify.

labels.name: Neither
labels.description: The available aims support neither definition, for example extending battery life or studying leaf senescence. Absence of a search keyword alone does not establish this label.

labels.name: Ambiguous
labels.description: The two definitions compete without a clear primary aim, or the available text does not support a choice. Use the separate low-confidence checkbox when missing text or uncertainty limits your judgment. A clearly documented boundary case can be ambiguous without low confidence.

confidence_note: Low confidence is independent of category. It records uncertainty about your judgment, including missing or truncated text. It is not a probability.
validation_note: No external check on the classifier. No validated funding estimate. A 90% human-agreement target remains a future criterion, not a measured result or an automatic publication gate.
